course.previewDescription: Explore how states rose, belief systems spread, trade networks connected regions, and revolutions reshaped societies from c. 1200 to the present.

unit.title: Consequences of Industrialization

themes.title: Interactions of humans with the environment
themes.question: How did geography, crops, resources, or disease shape choices?
themes.example: Andean terraces made steep slopes more usable for farming.

themes.title: Social interactions and organization
themes.question: Who had status, opportunities, or obligations?
themes.example: Examination preparation favored families that could afford education.

themes.title: Political systems and governance
themes.question: How did rulers gain authority and administer territory?
themes.example: Song officials carried imperial decisions into local government.

themes.title: Economic systems
themes.question: How were goods produced, exchanged, taxed, or distributed?
themes.example: Mali drew revenue from commerce through its territory.

themes.title: Cultural developments and interactions
themes.question: How did beliefs, learning, and artistic practices influence society?
themes.example: Buddhist monasteries connected religious practice with education.

themes.title: Technology and innovation
themes.question: What techniques or tools changed what people could do?
themes.example: Inca roads and knotted records helped officials coordinate resources.

questions.prompt: Which of the following best describes the relationship between industrialization and imperialism?
choices: Industrialization gave states motives for empire but not the means to expand
Industrialization gave states both motives and means to build empires
Imperialism caused industrialization to begin in Britain
Industrialization ended imperial expansion
questions.explanation: Industry created needs for raw materials and the technology to conquer.
choiceExplanations: It provided the means as well.
Industry created needs for raw materials and the technology to conquer.
Industrialization began before the new imperialism.
questions.distinguisher: Industry also provided the means: steamships, guns, and telegraphs.

questions.prompt: Which of the following claims about the imperial age is most defensible?
choices: Imperialism ended most migration between continents
Imperialism reshaped economies and populations beyond Europe
Imperialism affected only the economies of European states
Imperialism had no lasting effects after the colonies ended
questions.explanation: Export economies, migration, and racial ideas spread worldwide.
choiceExplanations: Imperialism spurred migration rather than ending it.
Export economies, migration, and racial ideas spread worldwide.
questions.distinguisher: Colonized economies were reshaped, so effects were not limited to Europe.

questions.prompt: The author's main argument is that industrialization
choices: gave a few states the power and motive to reshape the world
had little effect on societies outside Europe
ended racial ideas in Europe and America
reduced global migration across the oceans
questions.explanation: The author links industry to empire, export economies, migration, and racial ideas.
choiceExplanations: The author links industry to empire, export economies, migration, and racial ideas.
The passage says millions migrated in search of work.
questions.distinguisher: The author says effects reached far beyond Europe.

stimulusBlocks.source: CED Topic 6.8 key concept: causation in the imperial age, linking industrialization, imperialism, and migration
stimulusBlocks.attribution: Practice passage written for Page One, summarizing how industrialization shaped imperialism and migration, 1750–1900
stimulusBlocks.text:
Industrialization gave a few states unprecedented power. Their factories needed raw materials and markets, their steamships and telegraphs let them project power around the world, and their weapons gave them a decisive military advantage.

The results reached far beyond Europe. Colonized economies were reorganized to export raw materials, millions of people migrated in search of work, and imperial powers justified their rule with ideas of racial hierarchy that would shape the century to come.

questions.prompt: According to the passage, which of the following was an effect of imperialism?
choices: Industrial states lost their military advantage
Steamships were abandoned
Colonized economies industrialized faster than Europe
Colonized economies were reorganized to export raw goods
questions.explanation: The passage says colonized economies were reorganized for exports.
choiceExplanations: The passage says colonized economies were reorganized for exports.
questions.distinguisher: Colonized economies became raw material exporters.
